Apple is about to kick off a major new smart home push. Bloomberg published a report today revealing three brand-new smart home devices from Apple that are "nearly ready." The first two are expected to launch in just a few months…

Three brand-new Apple smart home products are nearly ready

According to the report, Apple will launch a new Apple TV set-top box and an updated HomePod mini this fall. These products will "look similar to the current versions" but will feature faster chips inside to support Apple Intelligence features.

For reference, the current Apple TV 4K uses the A15 Bionic chip. The current HomePod mini uses the S5 chip, the same processor used in the Apple Watch Series 5.

Even more exciting, Apple's long-awaited next-generation smart home hub is also "nearly ready." According to the report, the product is expected to debut "between October and early next year."

There are currently two versions of the product in development. One has "the screen on a hemispherical base," while the other is designed to "attach to the wall using a new magnetic system."

Today's report also revisits the device's specs and features. It's said to feature a 7-inch square display and be centered on Apple Intelligence. The device will run a "new operating system" based on tvOS, with an interface described as a "mix" of tvOS and watchOS, complete with apps, icons, and widgets.

It will also support FaceTime, home security monitoring, HomeKit integration, and Apple Watch-like custom watch faces.

However, the standout feature is expected to be facial recognition:

Finally, Bloomberg notes that Apple has two additional smart home products in development that will arrive later. These include a "premium robotic version of the smart home hub" with a 9-inch display, as well as an "advanced indoor security camera."
